name: Pit Fighters

specialRules.name: Leader
specialRules.description: Any models in the Warband within 6" of the King may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specialRules.name: Pit Fighter
specialRules.description: A Pit King has the Pit Fighter skill.

specialRules.name: Pit Fighter
specialRules.description: A Dwarf Troll Slayer has the Pit Fighter skill.

specialRules.name: Hard to Kill
specialRules.description: Dwarfs are tough, resilient individuals who can only be taken out of action on a roll of a 6 instead of 5-6 when rolling on the Injury chart. Treat a roll of 1-2 as knocked down, 3-5 as stunned, and 6 as out of action.

specialRules.name: Hard Head
specialRules.description: Dwarfs ignores the special rules for maces, clubs, etc. They are not easy to knock out!

specialRules.name: Hate Orcs and Goblins
specialRules.description: All Dwarfs hate Orcs and Goblins. See the psychology section of the Mordheim rules for details on the effects of hatred.

specialRules.name: Grudgebearers
specialRules.description: Dwarfs hold an ancient grudge against Elves from the days when the two races fought for the supremacy of the Old World. If the Pit Fighters ever hire any kind of Elven Hired Sword, he will leave the Warband immediately, he refuses to fight alongside these pansy Elves!

specialRules.name: Death Wish
specialRules.description: Troll Slayers seek an honourable death in combat. They are completely immune to all psychology

specialRules.name: Pit Fighter
specialRules.description: Pit Veterans have the Pit Fighter skill.

specialRules.name: Pit Fighter
specialRules.description: Pit Fighters have the Pit Fighter skill.

specialRules.name: Pit Fighter
specialRules.description: Pursuers have the Pit Fighter skill.

specialRules.name: Evade
specialRules.description: Pursuers are agile and athletic, well adept at avoiding the heavier Pit Fighters’ charges. When an enemy charges a Pursuer he may choose to try and evade. On a successful Initiative test it is considered a failed charge and the normal rules apply

specialRules.name: Pit Fighter
specialRules.description: An Ogre Pit Fighter has the Pit Fighter skill.

specialRules.name: Fear
specialRules.description: Ogre Pit Fighters are large, threatening creatures that cause fear.

specialRules.name: Large
specialRules.description: Ogre Pit Fighters are huge, lumbering creatures and therefore make tempting targets for archers. Any model may shoot at the Ogre Pit Fighter, even if he is not the closest target.

specialRules.name: Skills
specialRules.description: An Ogre Pit Fighter who becomes a Hero as a result of The Lad’s Got Talent may choose from the Combat, Strength and Pit Fighter Special Skills.

specialRules.name: Slow Witted
specialRules.description: Although Ogres are capable of earning experience and bettering themselves, they are not the smartest creatures. Ogres only gain advances at half the rate of everyone else (ie, they must accrue twice as much experience as normal to get an advance).

exclusiveEquipment.name: Dwarf axe
exclusiveEquipment.rulesText:
Dwarf axes have an extra save modifier of -1, so a model with Strength 4 using a Dwarf axe has a -2 save modifier when he hits an opponent with the axe in close combat.

Dwarf axes offer an excellent balance of defence and offense. A model armed with a Dwarf axe may parry blows. When his opponent rolls to hit, the model armed with a Dwarf axe may roll a D6. If the score is greater than the highest to hit score of his opponent, the model has parried the blow and that attack is discarded. A model may not parry attacks made with double or more its own Strength - they are simply too powerful to be stopped. A model may not parry more than one attack in a single Close Combat phase; a model armed with two Dwarf axes (or a Dwarf axe and a sword, etc) does not get to parry two attacks but may instead re-roll a failed parry.

specialRules: Pit Fighter: All Pit Fighters have the Pit Fighter skill as described in the Strength Skill List (+1 WS, +1 A when fighting in ruins, buildings and The Pit). | Hired Swords: Pit Fighters may hire all Hired Swords available except for the Elf Ranger, who feels working with such dirty and brutish individuals would just not do! | Weapons & Armour: Unlike other warbands that may chose which weapons and armour to equip their warriors with, Pit Fighters have to chose a specific fighting style which dictates their weapons and armour configuration. This is with the exception of Trollslayers and Ogres that may chose from a limited selection of equipment. The fighting style does not restrict Heroes from using items not on their list if they learn the appropriate skills. Pit Fighters may chose to change their fighting style at any stage by either swapping with another warrior in the warband or by simply buying a new style (or the separate components). Pit Fighter warbands also differ from other warbands in that a Henchman group may contain a mix of several different fighting styles and does not have to equip all of its warriors in the same manner. | Free the Slaves!: Pit Fighters hate all slavers. The Pit Fighters will never sell their captured opponents to the slavers. | In the Pit!: Pit Fighters who capture an opponent may decide to let him fight in the infamous fighting pits of Cutthroat’s Haven (use the rules that appeared earlier in this magazine). The Pit Fighter warband may decide to send in one or more of their own fighters to fight the captive. If the Pit Fighter wins, he gains +2 Experience, the warband gets all the captive’s armour and weapons +50gc. If the Pit Fighter loses, then roll to see whether he is dead or injured as normal (ignore all following results: Robbed, Captured, Hardened, Sold to the Pits, and Survives against the Odds). He will not lose his armour or weapons. The captive will get the 50gc and the +2 Experience when he wins. If the captive wins, the audience decides whether he gains his freedom. Roll a D6; on a 4+ the audience raises their thumbs and he is free. A 1-3 means he remains the Pit Fighters’ captive and may be fielded in the pits after future games.
